A new open-source tool has recently gone viral because it promises to let users who aren't interested in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Mac. Details below.

"Disable Apple Intelligence and remove downloaded models on macOS 27"

Like many companies that have added AI tools and models to their platforms, Apple has faced criticism for features some users view as superfluous taking up storage space.

Apple Intelligence requires up to 7GB of storage on macOS 26, but that figure has increased substantially with macOS 27, where Apple now says its latest models can require up to 14GB on newer Macs.

In response, independent developer Om Lahore released a project on GitHub late last week called RemoveMacAI, which claims to "disable Apple Intelligence and remove downloaded models on macOS 27".

Lahore explained that his tool can enable a configuration profile that applies Apple's own restriction keys to turn off Apple Intelligence functionality, while using the company's resource services to remove downloaded models and prevent macOS from downloading them again.

He also detailed what the tool removes and disables, as well as what users can expect after running it:

Disabled features: Siri (including "Hey Siri" and the menu bar icon), Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, ChatGPT extensions, summaries for Mail, Messages, Safari, Notes, and notifications, Mail smart replies, inline text prediction, spatial photos, photo cleanup, and Xcode predictive code completion. Removed models: the Apple Intelligence foundation model, as well as models used for image generation and Genmoji, spatial photos, photo cleanup, and Xcode code completion.

and

Lahore noted that dictation will still work after running RemoveMacAI, as it "is a separate setting, and its speech models will not be removed".

Finally, he added that the entire process is reversible, with full details and instructions available here.

9to5Mac's take

While some of the strong pushback over how much storage Apple Intelligence takes up on Mac seems like a reflexive aversion to anything AI-related, for users with limited storage—especially those with just 256GB Macs—reclaiming 12GB or more of space can make a real difference, which is a reasonable argument.

There's also the larger question of basic control over one's own operating system—users who have no interest in Apple Intelligence should have a straightforward way to turn it off entirely and reclaim the storage its models occupy, just as they can with other apps and system optional components.

That said, it's unknown whether Apple will try to take this project down from GitHub, or change the underlying mechanisms in macOS to make Apple Intelligence models harder to remove.

Similarly, it's also unclear what impact disabling or removing these components might have on macOS itself going forward, potentially affecting third-party apps that increasingly rely on Apple models to provide core functionality.

Although RemoveMacAI is open source and does not require disabling System Integrity Protection (SIP), it still relies on configuration profiles, restriction keys, and system services that Apple can change at any time.

That means future macOS updates could break parts of its functionality, or result in some unexpected behavior for users before the project can be updated.

For now, anyone considering using RemoveMacAI should understand that this is an unofficial third-party tool that makes system-level changes, and should be comfortable with how it operates.

Ultimately, to be clear, RemoveMacAI looks like a well-intentioned open-source project aimed at giving Mac users more autonomy and control over what runs on their computer and how their storage is used. It's just impossible to know whether Apple will view it the same way.
